usageNotes: Use this to add an IP address, CIDR block, or IP alias to an existing IPSet on a VM's firewall; the IPSet must already exist before entries can be added. The `nomatch` flag inverts the entry's match logic, useful for carving out exceptions within a broader CIDR. Requires `VM.Config.Network` permission on the target VM.

examples.summary: Add a trusted management CIDR to an IPSet named 'mgmt-allow' on VM 105

tips: The IPSet `name` must match pattern [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\-\_]+ — it must start with a letter and be 2–64 characters.
The `cidr` field accepts a plain IP (e.g. 192.168.1.5), a CIDR (e.g. 10.0.0.0/8), or a named alias defined in the firewall alias list.
Set `nomatch: true` to add a negation entry — useful to exclude a sub-range from a broader CIDR already in the set.
This call returns null on success; use get_nodes_node_qemu_vmid_firewall_ipset_name to verify the entry was added.
VM-level IPSets are local to that VM; cluster-level IPSets live under /cluster/firewall/ipset and must be managed separately.
